proposals.before: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
proposals.after: I have dwelt in your state a long time; I regret not killing you [the extant text 恨不殺汝 is probably corrupt (晉書斠注): the Tongjian reads 恨恨不欲殺汝, “with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you”; Yulan 744, quoting the 前燕錄, reads 誓不殺汝, “I swear not to kill you”].
proposals.sourceReason: The proposed 'am unwilling to kill you' treats 恨不 as if it simply meant 'unwilling', which the scope explicitly rules out. Without any mark it also translates the Tongjian variant in place of the extant 恨不殺汝, which is an emendation made silently in English. The amendment keeps the word-by-word rendering of the extant text, 'I regret not killing you'. It adds the documented critical reading in brackets, citing 晉書斠注's judgment and both witnesses, and changes no Chinese. The first clause takes the proposal's wording, 'a long time'.

proposals.before: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!
proposals.after: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius welcomed Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a bottle gourd; Yi Yin also said, 'Whom may I not serve as ruler? What people may I not command?' If even sages and worthies acted thus, how much more should we!
proposals.sourceReason: The proposal rightly corrects the first clause, 何事非君, to 'Whom may I not serve as ruler?'. But it renders 何使非民 as 'Whose people may I not serve?', which is a definite misreading. In Mencius (萬章下 and 公孫丑上), 使 is Yi Yin employing or commanding the people: Zhu Xi glosses it 所使者無非民, and Legge translates 'What people may I not command?'. Serving is the role of the first clause; the second is about directing the people. The amendment changes only that clause and keeps the rest of the proposal word for word, including 匏瓜 (bottle gourd), 聖賢 (sages and worthies) and 況吾曹乎 (how much more our sort).

proposals.before: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!
proposals.after: Yu told his friend Cheng Pan: “Confucius welcomed Bi Xi’s summons and used the bottle gourd as a metaphor for himself; Yi Yin also said, ‘Whom may I not serve as ruler? What people may I not command?’ If even sages and worthies were like this, how much more our sort!
proposals.sourceReason: The proposal rightly corrects the first clause, 何事非君, to 'Whom may I not serve as ruler?'. But it renders 何使非民 as 'Whose people may I not serve?', which is a definite misreading. In Mencius (萬章下 and 公孫丑上), 使 is Yi Yin employing or commanding the people: Zhu Xi glosses it 所使者無非民, and Legge translates 'What people may I not command?'. Serving is the role of the first clause; the second is about directing the people. The amendment changes only that clause and keeps the rest of the proposal word for word, including 匏瓜 (bottle gourd), 聖賢 (sages and worthies) and 況吾曹乎 (how much more our sort).

proposals.before: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
proposals.after: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—in both he took part in the planning; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
proposals.sourceReason: In 皆豫其謀, 豫 stands for 與 and means to take part in. Yu took part in the planning of both campaigns. 'Pre-planned their strategies' misreads 豫 as 'beforehand'. The idiomatic field already says 'He helped plan' correctly, so only that clause in the literal field changes.

units.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
units.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.
units.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.

units.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
units.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.
units.en: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.

units.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。
units.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.
units.en: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.

units.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
units.literal: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
units.en: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.

units.zh: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。
units.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
units.en: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.

units.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
units.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;
units.en: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;

units.zh: 不中者，可來前也。」
units.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”
units.en: if I miss, come on.”

units.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。
units.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.
units.en: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.

units.zh: 時鮮卑單于段眷為晉驃騎大將軍、遼西公，雅好人物，虛心延裕。
units.literal: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.
units.en: At that time the Xianbei shanyu Duan Juan, who held the Jin titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi, had a refined fondness for men of talent and humbly invited Yang Yu.

units.zh: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！
units.literal: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!
units.en: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!

units.zh: 眷今召我，豈徒然哉！」
units.literal: Juan now summons me—how could it be vain!”
units.en: Duan Juan’s summons is no empty gesture!”

units.zh: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
units.literal: Pan said: “Now Huaxia split and crumbling, the nine provinces in tatters, where tracks reach is only to the Yi River.
units.en: Cheng Pan replied, “Now Huaxia is split and crumbling, the nine provinces torn apart; where proper tracks reach is only as far as the Yi River.

units.zh: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
units.literal: To wish to live in proud reclusion (as in the “Kao pan”) and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
units.en: To wish to live in proud reclusion and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.

units.zh: 人壽幾何？
units.literal: Human life how much?
units.en: How long is a life?

units.zh: 古人以為白駒之歎。
units.literal: The ancients took this as the white colt’s sigh.
units.en: The ancients sighed at time’s white colt.

units.zh: 少遊有雲，郡掾足以廕後，況國相乎！
units.literal: Shao You said, a commandery aide suffices to shade posterity—how much more a state chancellor!
units.en: Shaoyou said that a post as commandery clerk was enough to shelter one's descendants; how much more the post of chancellor of a state!

units.zh: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」
units.literal: You trace Yi and Kong, or also know the moment’s spirit.”
units.en: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”

units.zh: 裕乃應之。
units.literal: Yu thereupon answered him.
units.en: Yang Yu accepted Duan Juan’s offer.

units.zh: 拜郎中令、中軍將軍，處上卿位。
units.literal: Appointed Palace Director, Central Army General, occupying the upper minister’s seat.
units.en: He was named palace director and central army general, ranking among the highest ministers.

units.zh: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。
units.literal: Passed through serving the Duan house’s five lords, greatly was respected.
units.en: He served five successive Duan lords and won deep respect.

units.zh: 段遼之請迎于季龍也，裕以左丞領征東麻秋司馬。
units.literal: When Duan Liao requested that Jilong receive him, Yu, as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.
units.en: When Duan Liao asked Shi Hu to send troops to receive him, Yang Yu, while serving as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.

units.zh: 秋敗，裕為軍人所執，將詣皝。
units.literal: When Qiu was defeated, Yu was seized by soldiers, was about to be brought to Huang.
units.en: Ma Qiu’s defeat left Yang Yu a prisoner on his way to Murong Huang.

units.zh: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
units.literal: Huang had long heard of Yu’s name; immediately ordered his bonds released; appointed Palace Director; promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
units.en: Murong Huang, who had long heard of Yu’s name, at once ordered his bonds released, appointed him Palace Director, then promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.

units.zh: 東破高句麗，北滅宇文歸，皆豫其謀，皝甚器重之。
units.literal: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
units.en: He helped plan the eastern victory over Goguryeo and the northern destruction of Yuwen Gui, and Huang came to rely on him heavily.

units.zh: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。
units.literal: When moved the capital to Helong, Yu by nature had clever thought; the city walls and palace towers Huang regulated were all Yu’s models.
units.en: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.

units.zh: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。
units.literal: Although Yu served Huang daily nearer, favor and rank above the old men’s, nature humble and respectful, clear and frugal, firm, simple, kind, and earnest; although passed through dwelling at court’s apex, like a scholar in plain cloth.
units.en: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.

units.zh: 士大夫流亡羈絕者，莫不經營收葬，存恤孤遺，士無賢不肖皆傾身待之，是以所在推仰。
units.literal: Grandees and scholars who fled in exile and were cut off—none he did not arrange burial for, preserve and pity orphans left behind; gentry whether worthy or not all he inclined his person to treat; therefore wherever he was was pushed and looked up to.
units.en: He buried exiles, aided their orphans, and honored every gentleman he met, winning universal esteem.

references.title: 晉書斠注 七十一v109–110
references.quote: 《晉書》校文五曰《御覽》七百四十四引前燕錄作誓不殺汝詳語意崔錄似得其眞又攷《通鑑》作恨恨不欲殺汝注恨恨相戀之情與誓字語意正合此語温公必有所本疑恨不殺汝四字卽恨恨不欲殺汝一語之譌脫
何事非君，何使非民；治亦進，亂亦進，伊尹也。
references.reason: Check service of a ruler versus employing/commanding the people, not serving them.
